reviewer_independence: Performed by a separate evidence-audit agent that did not implement or edit the candidate source.
scope: Frozen one-process, 32-tenant, volatile-recovery embedded-v3 workload only.

dependency_facts.product_runtime: extism 1.30.0 from crates.io with default features disabled and only wasmtime-default-features
dependency_facts.scheduler: one std::thread tenant worker per ready tenant; no candidate Tokio runtime

checks.evidence: Each ready tenant has its own bounded sync_channel and OS worker thread. Guest execution is not protected by a global execution lock; only the required single NDJSON writer is globally serialized.
checks.observation: The architecture uses 32 long-lived tenant threads for the frozen population, so this result cannot be extrapolated to actor densities far above the preregistered workload.

checks.evidence: GuestCatalog compiles each hash-pinned artifact once and reuses CompiledPlugin handles for instantiation.
checks.observation: A successful rollout instantiates and discards one preflight plugin per target, then instantiates a second replacement per target after freeze. Keeping the preflight replacements would remove this duplicate instantiation, but the frozen run must measure the reviewed code as written.

checks.evidence: The adapter uses Extism PluginBuilder and CompiledPlugin rather than constructing a separate Wasmtime Engine per tenant or command. Core artifacts are compiled once, and the hash-pinned guest declares memory 1 1.

The candidate uses Extism's maintained plugin compilation, instantiation, host-function, and cancellation APIs. The actor lifecycle, admission, idempotency, recovery, and rollout layer is necessarily candidate adapter code in this comparison.

Both core and authority PluginBuilder paths call with_wasi(false). Only comparison custom functions are registered. Five foreign ABI probes require exact unknown-import failures, while the native Extism HTTP canary must reach the explicit no-http policy denial at invocation.
Trap and CancelHandle CPU-deadline failures are handled inside the target tenant worker, followed by target-only Plugin replacement, incarnation advance, and volatile-state reset.

All target activations are preflighted before freeze. Failed preflight leaves running instances unchanged; successful preflight freezes all targets, creates all replacements, and reports InDoubt on a failed swap rather than false commit.

known_limitations: The one-thread-per-tenant architecture is acceptable only for the frozen 32-tenant lane and is not evidence of high actor density.
Successful rollout performs duplicate preflight and replacement instantiation.
The candidate has zero Tokio worker threads; any run-manifest rule requiring four Tokio workers for every candidate would be factually incompatible with this implementation.
Passing this static review is permission to run the frozen experiment, not evidence that its dynamic gates or SLOs pass.
